versions.changelog:
Summary: Adds advanced voice customization options and updates documentation for the ClawVoice skill.

- Adds support for customizing agent voice (ID, language, tier, preset, mix, expression, expression level, and controls) via setup and CLI.
- Expands setup and command-line options to include voice customization flags (e.g., --voice, --lang, --preset).
- Updates agent rules to guide users on changing voice and related settings with `clawvoice voice`.
- Enhances documentation for push-to-talk, mic support, and hosted/local voice selection.
- No breaking changes to existing commands or wallet controls.

- Added lib/playback.js module.
- Updated agent rules to clarify branding: Preferred CLI is now clawvoice, with agentvoice/x402-agent-voice as compatibility aliases.
- Users can now use clawvoice stop to immediately stop speaking on command.
- Expanded "Agent Rules" to cover user requests to stop voice, reinforce session logic, and clarify command triggers.
- Updated command list to include stop command and improved naming consistency.

- Added scripts/test-python-probe.js for additional Python runtime probing.
- Updated agent rules in SKILL.md to clarify when and how to use ClawVoice for speaking replies.
- Improved session voice mode instructions and sensitive content handling guidance in the documentation.

- Updated the display name to "ClawVoice Agent Voice + TTS" for clarity.
- Improved the short description to emphasize voice and TTS for OpenClaw agents.
- No code or command changes; documentation only.

- Added new file: lib/python.js
- Updated skill description for improved clarity and brevity
- Bumped version to 0.3.9

- Adds detailed SKILL.md documentation on usage, setup, wallet rules, security, and voice/mic installation.
- Clarifies that ClawVoice provides both local TTS agent voice and a local x402 Base wallet.
- Documents all commands, setup modes, and agent fee/cap policy.
- Outlines strict handling of private keys and spend limits for security.
- Expands references section for pricing, security, third-party attributions, and dependencies.
